newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: China promises Argentina investment via Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China promises Argentina investment via Hong Kong.

text.p: China promised Argentina Friday that it will receive an injection of Chinese investment through its new trading post of Hong Kong, and backed up the promise with a new credit line.

Chinese Vice Premier Li Lanqing, visiting Buenos Aires on a tour of Latin America, said in comments carried by state-run Argentine news agency Telam: "China is now entering a phase of foreign investment and is ready to invest in Argentina."
"Argentines will be welcome through Hong Kong," said the senior Chinese official, calling his country's recovery of the British-run territory in June "an incomparable advantage."

During Li Lanqing's meeting Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, the Chinese Import and Export Bank and Argentina's Foreign Investment and Commerce Bank (BICE) signed an agreement opening up a Chinese credit line for Argentina.

The credit line, for loans of an unspecified amount for a maximum term of 10 years, is aimed at financing imports of capital goods from China and will cover up to 85 percent of the value of the import transaction.

Earlier in the day, Li Lanqing met Argentina's President Carlos Menem. Argentina officials said the two "analyzed the possibilities of increasing the flow of investment between the two countries and creating closer commercial ties."
Argentina's Foreign Ministry said in a statement that two-way trade with China had grown to $1.3 billion last year from $298 million in 1992.

"China has become the top buyer of Argentine products in the Asia-Pacific region, accounting for 21 percent of our sales to the area," said the Argentine ministry, adding that Argentina's main exports to China are animal feed and animal, vegetable and seed oils .
Li Lanqing, on a tour also including Chile, Brazil, Paraguay and Colombia, is due to leave Argentina until Monday.
